Marathon Petroleum has climbed 8.23% over two weeks and gained another 0.18% today in a refining environment that's working in its favor. U.S. refineries are running at 98% capacity while oil inventories remain elevated at 711 million barrels—this tight utilization means refiner margins (the spread between what they pay for crude and what they earn from selling gasoline and diesel) tend to stay healthy. The backdrop has been escalating U.S.-Iran military tensions that have spiked crude prices 9% this week, with ongoing EU sanctions on Iranian oil tightening global supply.

The combination of high refinery utilization, elevated crude prices, and geopolitical friction over Iranian oil supply creates a favorable short-term environment for refiners like MPC. Even as broader economic uncertainty swirls—Argentina's renewed Falklands saber-rattling and U.S. sanctions expansion—oil remains scarce and refining capacity is running flat-out, which historically supports refiner profitability.
